top_signals.title: Citi's Hollenhorst Sees Trend Toward Cooling Inflation
top_signals.summary: Andrew Hollenhorst, chief US economist at Citi, discusses the outlook for today's US inflation report. "If we get a cool reading again this month, and we think that we will, then you have more of a trend toward cooling inflation," Hollenhorst tells Bloomberg Television. "And that's just a very, very different story than what we've been hearing from some Fed officials." (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: AI’s costly buildout complicates the Fed’s inflation fight
top_signals.summary: Tech leaders say AI will drive down costs. But slow corporate adoption and the data center buildout create inflation pressures that complicate the Fed’s job.
top_signals.why_it_matters: AI and semiconductor developments impacting technology leadership and capex cycles.

top_signals.title: India Inflation Stays Within Target Band, Backs RBI Pause
top_signals.summary: India’s inflation was broadly steady in July, holding within the Reserve Bank’s 2%-6% target range and cementing expectations policymakers will keep interest rates unchanged for some time.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Inflation expectations impacting rate path, bonds and global risk assets.

top_signals.title: Mortgage rates finally stop rising, causing demand to trickle back
top_signals.summary: Mortgage rates finally eased a tiny bit, but it was enough to bring some demand back to a very beleaguered mortgage market.
